title.narrative: Improved management of labour migration and reduction of irregular migration

description.narrative: According to UNDESA, Ethiopia’s net migration rate continues to be negative, and stood at -11,999 in 2022. Irregular migration remains very high and both regular and irregular migrants encounter a number of challenges and protection risks at every step of the journey starting from their place of origin as well as transit and destination countries. Recognizing the above challenges, the GoE, with the support of the ILO, has taken progressive steps to make migration a choice rather than a necessity. In this regard, the Ethiopian Overseas Employment program was launched which aims to create a safe, orderly & regular labour migration for Ethiopian workers abroad. Inspite of important legislative and policy breakthroughs over the past decade, the impact of adopted measures has remained limited, particularly in terms of ensuring actual protection, shifting significantly the share of irregular to regular migrant workers, and upscaling measures. This CPO proposes to improve existing services and enhance monitoring and review mechanisms of inter and intra-regional cooperation frameworks to protect the labour rights of migrant workers and seek stronger alignment with ILS. The strategy intended to be used in this regard include among others, strengthening the existing digitalized overseas employment process to ensure wider access; improving labour migration statistics and social protection coverage in Ethiopia; enhancing protection through BLAs and other inter and intra-regional cooperation frameworks in line with relevant ILS; facilitating negotiation, implementation and monitoring of BLAs as well as other cooperation frameworks. The interventions to achieve the CPO bring together the AU-ILO-IOM-ECA (JLMP-Action), (JLMP-Lead); BRMM, the project on reintegration of returnees in Addis Ababa and the Strengthening inter and intra-regional cooperation for safe, regular and orderly labour migration in Ethiopia and the Programme Implementation of the Djibouti Declaration.
